title: Number Guessing Game
story: 'I'm thinking of a number between 1 and 100...' The classic game that's been played on paper, in classrooms, and as a first programming project for decades. Build it complete: random number, guesses, hints (too high/too low), and score tracking.
why: The number guessing game combines random number generation, loops, conditionals, and user interaction into a complete, playable program.
analogy: Binary search in action: 'too high / too low' is exactly how a computer searches a sorted list. Each guess eliminates half the remaining numbers. The optimal strategy (bisection) finds any number in at most log₂(range) guesses. You're teaching the computer's own search strategy back to yourself.
try_it: Implement three difficulty levels that change the range and max attempts. Add a 'hint' system: give a divisibility hint on the 3rd wrong guess (e.g., 'the number is even'). Track best score across multiple games.
tips: Use binary search for optimal play: guess the midpoint each time
Track attempts as the primary score metric — fewer attempts = better
Give clear hints: 'too high' and 'too low' are the universal language of this game
common_mistakes: Not updating the search range after a wrong guess — binary search requires it
Counting the winning guess as 'too many' — include it in the attempt count
Using a range that grows too fast — keep difficulty linear: easy=small range, hard=big range
